findings.message: Bare `except:` with `pass` swallows all exceptions (including GatewayError and programming errors) instead of raising PaymentError; callers expecting PaymentError will no longer see it.
findings.suggestion: Restore the specific handler, e.g. `except GatewayError as exc: raise PaymentError(f"charge failed for order {order.id}: {exc}") from exc` (and do not catch bare exceptions).

findings.message: If `charge(...)` raises, the exception is swallowed and execution reaches `return result` with `result` unbound, producing an UnboundLocalError/NameError that masks the real failure instead of a PaymentError.
findings.suggestion: Do not return after a swallowed exception; either re-raise/convert to PaymentError or initialize/handle `result` explicitly and fail loudly on error.
